summary: This claude-control-only diff is additive and low-risk: it expands ai-os/VARIABLE_DICTIONARY_2026-07-24.yaml from 60 to all 444 catalog tables (mechanical, generator-produced metadata) and adds a new standalone tool script (ai-os-scripts/phase5_generate_full_repo_exemptions.py) that is meant to be run against a separate compliance-tracker checkout; neither file touches .github/workflows/**, migrations, schema, auth, or secrets paths, and the diff is insertion-dominated (66848 added vs 7377 deleted), so tier1 classification is correct. I verified the new VARIABLE_DICTIONARY_SOURCE_ROWS_2026-07-24.json contains only dev/seed/demo Supabase rows (org_001='Acme Corp', test/demo emails and phone numbers, a synthetic-looking GSTIN) with sensitive columns (password_hash, passcode_hash) properly redacted before use, not real production PII, and the worker's own result.json/task.yaml checkpoints are honest about scope: it explicitly did NOT mark TERMINOLOGY_STANDARDIZATION_PHASE_PLAN_2026-07-24.yaml's phase_5 entry done, did NOT attempt to push the compliance-tracker ci.yml change itself (correctly deferred given the known workflow-scope/OAuth limitation), and left the real cross-repo deliverable (CI widening + exemptions-manifest regeneration) in an open, unmerged compliance-tracker PR #554 rather than falsely claiming it complete from a claude-control-only diff -- which is exactly the discipline the phase plan's own process_notes.cross_repo_review_gap demands after a prior violation of that rule. One non-blocking design concern worth follow-up when PR #554 itself is reviewed: the generator script's PROSE_EXAMPLE_REASON/CODE_LITERAL_REASON boilerplate strings assert 'confirmed on direct read' / 'spot-checked this phase' for every matching finding, but the docstring's actual investigation only names a handful of representative files -- that reasoning is then applied programmatically, unverified, to potentially thousands of individual findings across 2079 files, which risks the compliance-tracker exemptions baseline overclaiming verification it didn't really do per-instance.
issues: ai-os-scripts/phase5_generate_full_repo_exemptions.py's build_reason() emits a canned 'confirmed on direct read' / 'spot-checked this phase' justification for every finding matching a category+file-type heuristic, but only a handful of files were actually spot-checked per the script's own docstring -- this blanket-applies an unverified claim across potentially thousands of findings in the compliance-tracker exemptions baseline it generates (relevant to the separate, still-open compliance-tracker PR #554, not to this claude-control diff directly).

Minor dead code in the same script: the final print statement's `sum(c for _, c in counts.items()) if False else report['summary']['total_findings']` has an unreachable branch (harmless, but should be simplified to just the report value).
